rig_validation_detail.finding: no pair collapsed — matte/glossy, glossy/metallic, opaque/transparent and opaque/translucent all still pass, and glossy/metallic clears all six axes. The single failure is METAL_METALLIC at scene-linear peak 0.114, BELOW the 0.35 lower bound, with ZERO clipping.
rig_validation_detail.why_it_matters: the window's lower bound exists so a measurement has signal above noise. At 0.114 with zero clipping the METAL measurement is not corrupted, and glossy/metallic still separates on all six axes — but a characterization rig that cannot put a metal in its own operating band is not yet a general-purpose M5/M6 asset, which is what §3 asks for.
rig_validation_detail.corrected: an earlier note in this record said metal exceeded the window. It does the opposite. A metallic surface reflects its ENVIRONMENT rather than scattering light back, and this rig has a near-black backdrop by design — so metal has almost nothing to reflect and renders dark. The compact source gives it one small highlight and nothing else.
rig_validation_detail.real_fix: give the rig a declared reflection environment — a neutral gradient or a small set of emissive cards the metal can reflect — rather than lowering the window. Metals are characterised against what they reflect; a black room is not a characterization environment.
